questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Selection of courses, culture of the city and ranking of university

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The university, student houseing and ESN were a great help and would answer must of my questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university of Amsterdam would provide me with the essential information about how to travel, registration etc. My student housing were also helpful with any questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not easy. it was difficult to understand the process of student housing and when it was time to select housing it was very stressful.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is difficult to find something affordable on the private market so start looking a while before going abroad. Furthermore, be aware of the student housing deadlines from the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was very easy. University of Amsterdam has a digital portal were all the information and documentation is uploaded. They are also very helpful with questions.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They have an email you can write to and lots of information on their website.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful, I got all the courses that I selected.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware of the english reqiurements.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The levels of the courses are high but not more difficult than the level from University of Copenhagen. You have to read more than you are used to.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is the same teaching style as at the University of Copenhagen. Lectures with around 60-80 students and seminars with around 20-30 students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Foundations of EU competition law, European company law, EU Private International Law, European tort law and making markets beyond the state.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Foundations of EU competition law. The professor is very good and the course have a big relevans for working with law in Denmark. It gives a great overview of competition law in general.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: My bike got stolen so I needed to buy a new one. Transportation was more expensive than expected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and drinks are a little less expensive then in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I did not participate in any activities at my host institution.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There are many markets and festivals in Amsterdam during the spring / summer, which is very fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Amsterdam have many parks and nice cafés you can visit on your own or with friends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy. The Dutch people are very welcoming and good at English.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the events planned by the UvA and ESN Amsterdam.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They do not use handsignals when biking.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very friendly and enjoy being outside when the weather is nice. There are many nice spots by the canals in the city where you can hang out.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get a bike. It is much easier and cheaper. The public transport is not going after 1am and it is therefore nice to have a bike when going home. The UvA is very helpful, if any questions they will answer within a day or two.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: When studying law you order "readers" with the case law and legislation. This is what you are allowed to bring to an exam if you have open book exams. You have to order this yourself online and it cost extra.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from diffrent countries and learning about how it is to be students there.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being more outgoing and meeting people that are very diffrent from me.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
